content: Valacyclovir is a medication prescribed to treat herpes zoster (commonly known as shingles) and genital herpes. While it does not cure herpes infections, it helps reduce pain and itching, promotes the healing of sores, and prevents the formation of new sores. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Valacyclovir is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For the treatment of shingles, it is typically taken three times a day (every 8 hours) for a duration of 7 days. For genital herpes, it is usually taken twice daily for 5 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and if you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take valacyclovir exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Begin using this medication as soon as symptoms appear. Even if you feel better, continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration. Do not stop taking valacyclovir without consulting your doctor. Before starting valacyclovir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acyclovir (Zovirax), valacyclovir, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including cimetidine (Tagamet), probenecid (Benemid), and any vitamins or supplements. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, immune system problems, HIV infection, or AIDS. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking valacyclovir, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose of valacyclovir, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Valacyclovir may cause side effects. Mild side effects include headache, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea or loose stools, and constipation. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention and include rash, itching, confusion, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fever, and blood in the urine. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store valacyclovir in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and undergo any laboratory tests they recommend to monitor your response to valacyclovir. Avoid sexual intercourse when visible genital herpes lesions are present, as the infection can still be transmitted even when no symptoms are apparent. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription or if symptoms persist after completing the course of valacyclovir, contact your doctor. The brand name for valacyclovir is Valtrex® Caplets.
